clue.text: Set right, and it gets her flustered

indicators.note: being flustered leaves one in a muddle, so the letters of these words get thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone corrects a situation, and a woman is left rattled by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flustered' rearranges all of AND IT GETS HER; the comma makes 'and' look like a joining word, but it supplies the A, N and D.
explanation.definitionFit: To straighten something out is to correct it or put it in order.

clue.text: Charge for holding the boards without an alternative

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the stage word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: the boards is a theatre term for the stage
or is the word that introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A fee for keeping planks, offered with no other option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage is also the fee a warehouse makes for keeping goods.

clue.text: Strip, lock stock and barrel

explanation.surface: Someone stripping everything, the whole lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock stock and barrel' looks like the idiom for everything, but here it lists the lock, stock and barrel, the three main parts of a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to ransack and strip it; lock, stock and barrel are the parts of a long gun.

clue.text: Being cheeky about the Right is not wise!

indicators.note: about means around, so the cheeky word goes around the other piece

parts.note: being cheeky means impudent
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A political jibe: being rude about the right wing is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IMPUDENT around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent is a synonym for unwise or rash.

clue.text: Greet distantly

parts.note: a greeting called out to someone far away, as to a ship within calling range

explanation.definitionFit: To hail someone is to call out a greeting to them from a distance.

clue.text: Attractive binding

explanation.surface: A charming way of tying things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaging means charming; to engage oneself is to commit or bind, so engaging is binding.

clue.text: Scoff about class and social distinction

indicators.note: about means around, so the scoff word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to scoff is to eat greedily
CL is the abbreviation for class

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at the class system and at those with social standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' looks like mockery, but here it means to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliant success or acclaim, a mark of standing in society.

clue.text: Hold back — shower after all the others

indicators.note: after places the shower word following the other piece

parts.note: the rest means all the others
a shower is a fall of rain

explanation.surface: Advice to wait before taking a shower until everyone else has had theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' looks like a wash, but it is a fall of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to check or keep in check.

clue.text: He acts badly though really decent

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of these words are put together wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A man behaves poorly though he is basically a good person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges HE ACTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and modest, decent in the strictest sense.

clue.text: Children not being served well

parts.note: a dish that is off is no longer available on the menu
a spring is a well, a source of water

explanation.surface: Kids are not being looked after properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like an adverb, but it is the noun meaning a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are a person's children or young.

clue.text: An old doctor given shelter by the church

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side away from the wind
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A doctor of former times finds sanctuary in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is only a joining word between the doctor and the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Leech was an archaic word for a physician, from the bloodsuckers they applied.

clue.text: A rendezvous for explorers?

parts.note: a place where explorers meet; but the idiom says one explores every possibility, a route or line of enquiry

explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a line of approach, and we speak of exploring every one.

clue.text: Finding it in an article entrances and excites

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in places the piece it into the entrances word

parts.note: gates are entrances

explanation.surface: Discovering something within a news article thrills its reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a piece of writing, but it is the grammatical indefinite article.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to stir up or disturb, as to excite does.

clue.text: One's double

parts.note: not a lookalike but the digit one written twice side by side

explanation.definitionFit: The number written 11 is the numeral 1 repeated.

clue.text: Obtain switch out of the petty cash

parts.note: ex is the Latin word for out of
loose change is petty cash

explanation.surface: Get someone to swap you money from the office float.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange is to give one thing and get another in its place.

clue.text: The batsman's position is swell

explanation.surface: The cricketer's stance is great.
explanation.walkthrough: A batsman who is 'in his crease' is safe in cricket, the line marking his ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the batting term means safely behind the batting line; as one word it means to grow or swell.

clue.text: Vindicate a course of action without hesitation

parts.note: to right a wrong is to vindicate or set it straight
a way is a method or course of action

explanation.surface: Justifying a chosen plan at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight away means immediately, with no delay.

clue.text: Scholarly people retail it in a diverting way

indicators.note: diverting means turning aside, so the letters of these words are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Academics sell their knowledge in an entertaining manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverting' looks like amusing, but signals rearranging RETAIL IT.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are well-read, educated people.

clue.text: A seafood appetiser perhaps, with a bird to follow

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
to tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A menu: prawn starter followed by poultry for the main course.
explanation.walkthrough: A prawn cocktail is a classic British starter, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prawn cocktail is one type of mixed starter or drink.

clue.text: Bank giving many a cautious signal

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, taken as many
the amber traffic light tells drivers to take care

explanation.surface: A riverbank sends out a warning sign to many.
explanation.definitionFit: A camber is the banked slope of a road surface.

clue.text: An aged eccentric listed matters to be discussed

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of these words are set in a new order

explanation.surface: An elderly oddball draws up a list of things to talk about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' looks like a description of the old person but rearranges AN AGED.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the list of items for a meeting.

clue.text: Plain tea, sure as can be!

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters of these words may be made into something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinker insists their tea is as unadorned as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges TEA SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means severe and simple, without ornament.

clue.text: Certainly in drink, as determined by the rule

indicators.note: in places the certainty word inside the drink word

parts.note: mead is a drink made from honey
sure means certainly

explanation.surface: Someone drunk swears they acted entirely according to regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rule' is a measuring ruler here, not a regulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something measured has been gauged with a ruler.

clue.text: Free in the Home Counties

indicators.note: in says the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something available at no charge around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties around London.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie is to set loose or free.

clue.text: Craft gallery in the USA

indicators.note: in places the gallery word within the craft piece

parts.note: SS stands for steamships, sea craft
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: An American workshop showcasing handmade work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft gallery' suggests a crafts shop; 'Craft' is ships, SS, with the Tate (London gallery) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The States is the everyday name for America.

clue.text: Taste a port in Tanzania

parts.note: a tang is a sharp taste

explanation.surface: Sample a harbour town in East Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanga is a seaport city in northern Tanzania.

clue.text: For squalid housing the total cost is about a pound

indicators.note: is about means is around, so the total word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a sum is a total
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling

explanation.surface: Run-down homes cost around a pound altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' puts SUM around L.
explanation.definitionFit: A slum is a run-down, overcrowded area of poor housing.

clue.text: Dined soundly at a reasonable hour

indicators.note: soundly signals it is how the past tense of eat sounds that counts

parts.note: dined means ate

explanation.surface: Someone had a good meal at a sensible time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like well, but signals a sound-alike: ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight o'clock is a sensible time for supper.

clue.text: Grant admission

explanation.surface: Permission to enter.
explanation.definitionFit: An allowance is a grant of money, and also an acknowledgement or concession.

clue.text: Old Nick can be solicitous, though unconcerned

parts.note: Old Nick is a nickname for Satan
may means can, be allowed to
to care is to be solicitous

explanation.surface: Even Satan can show kindness, though he couldn't care less.
explanation.definitionFit: Devil-may-care means reckless and carefree.
